detail.longDescription: I now feel that the math world will eventually become like the programming world: responsible for all kinds of strange hypotheses and creations. Then let AI verify them, do the work, get the results, and reinvent the wheel over and over again, but every wheel is made differently. There are millions of ways to implement a feature, and the same goes for proving a mathematical conjecture. I really miss the time before AI, the feeling of being immersed in writing code and the sense of achievement after completing a feature. And being able to happily share with others the methods I found during development and my design ideas. But now, I can only pursue features and rough design directions. It's become like having meetings with AI every day to discuss features. But I can't go back to the old-fashioned way of programming anymore, because I can no longer purely immerse myself in writing a program. Because I know that whatever I write, AI can do it in a few seconds, and do it better. I can't get any sense of achievement, and the time I spend becomes purely a waste of time. I've already given up now. I'm not some top student from a top university, or some top talent who has worked at a top company. The ambition I used to have is gone. All that's left is the thought of "destroy everything together, then create completely new rules and a new world."
